alternatives.title: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute alternatives in this catalogue
alternatives.description: Cordless vacuums in the catalogue whose maker pages can be read next to the V15 Detect Absolute: weight, run time, charge time, and the lines that only one page states.
alternatives.subject: dyson-v15-detect

sections.heading: What the V15 page actually states
paragraphs: The V15 Detect Absolute page states 6.83 lb, up to 60 min of run time, a 4.5 hr charge time, a 0.2 gallon bin, whole-machine HEPA filtration, and 230 AW in Boost mode. Those six lines are the whole spec card. An alternative in this catalogue is another cordless vacuum whose card prints a weight, a run time, or a charge time you can put next to those lines.

Three cards do that. The PURE ONE S15 PRO page states 6.8 lbs, 40 min, and 4 hours, plus a 2500 mAh battery and a 0.47 L dust capacity. The IP3251 page states 18.47 lbs, up to 70 minutes measured at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, and a 6 hour charge, plus a 0.7 qt dust cup, full-size dimensions, and 21.6 volts. The V8 page states 5.58 lb, 40 min maximum, a 5 hr charge, a 0.14 gallon bin, and 115 AW in MAX mode.

sections.heading: Pick by the line you are matching
paragraphs: Pick the V15 Detect Absolute if the run-time line you need is up to 60 min, the suction line is 230 AW in Boost mode, or the filtration line is whole-machine HEPA. The stated weight is 6.83 lb and the charge line is 4.5 hrs. Pick it when those are the figures on the box you are about to match, not because a page on this site ranked it.

Pick the PURE ONE S15 PRO if the weight you are matching is 6.8 lbs, the run time is 40 min, and the charge line is 4 hours, or you need the 2500 mAh battery line and the 0.47 L dust capacity. The weight sits next to the V15 line. The run time is shorter than the V15 line.

Pick the IP3251 if the run-time sentence you are matching is up to 70 minutes at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, and you can accept a stated weight of 18.47 lbs and a 6 hour charge. That run-time sentence names a configuration. It is not the same sentence as “up to 60 min” on the V15 page.

Pick the V8 if the weight you are matching is 5.58 lb, the run time is 40 min maximum, and the suction line is 115 AW in MAX mode. The bin on that page is 0.14 gallon, against 0.2 gallon on the V15 page. The charge line is 5 hrs, longer than the V15 charge line. Both are Dyson pages, and the numbers are not the same.

sections.heading: Notices that name a different model
paragraphs: The V15 and V8 cards link a Health Canada notice for a FirstPower replacement battery for Dyson V6 series vacuums. That notice names V6. It does not name the V15 Detect Absolute or the V8 card’s model line. Read the model on the notice before applying it.

The IP3251 card links the 2015 CPSC notice for Shark Rotator Lift-Away vacuums, models NV650W, NV651, NV652, and NV660, and the Health Canada notice that names NV650W and NV652. IP3251 is not those model numbers. The recall block on this page is the catalogue match for each of the four cards.

alternatives.title: Levoit Core 300S-P alternatives in this catalogue
alternatives.description: Air purifiers in the catalogue whose maker pages can be read next to the Core 300S-P: weight and cabinet on the small Levoit, CADR and room lines on the other cards.
alternatives.subject: levoit-core-300s-p

sections.heading: The 300S-P card is a small cabinet
paragraphs: The Core 300S-P manual states AC 120 V, 60 Hz, 39 W, noise of 22–54.5 dB, dimensions of 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in, and a weight of 7.48 lb. It does not print a CADR label or a room-size label. An alternative on this page is a purifier card that does print a room or CADR line, or the larger Levoit that prints both.

The Airmega Mighty AP-1512HH page states CADR of 233 smoke, 246 dust, and 240 pollen, room coverage of 361 ft² at 4.8 air changes per hour, dimensions of 16.8 × 18.3 × 9.6 in, a weight of 12.3 lb, and 77 W. The Core 600S-P page states 391 CFM, 13.7 lb, 12.3 x 12.3 x 23.6 in, 49 W, noise of 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker), and a room line of 2,909 sq ft at 1 air change per hour or 606 sq ft at 4.8. The Blue Pure 211i Max page states a recommended room of 674 sq ft, 22.7 x 14.4 x 14.4 in, 16.2 lb, and sound of 23 to 53 dB.

sections.heading: Pick by cabinet weight or by a room line
paragraphs: Pick the Core 300S-P if the cabinet you are matching is 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in at 7.48 lb and the power line is 39 W. The noise line is a range, 22–54.5 dB. Pick it when you do not need a CADR figure from the same page, because this card does not have one.

Pick the AP-1512HH if you need a CADR trio and a room line that names 361 ft² at 4.8 air changes per hour. The stated weight is 12.3 lb and the power line is 77 W, both higher than the 300S-P lines. The cabinet is larger in two of the three dimensions.

Pick the Core 600S-P if the figure you need is 391 CFM or the room line that names 606 sq ft at 4.8 air changes, in a 12.3 x 12.3 x 23.6 in cabinet at 13.7 lb. The noise line on that page is 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker). The 300S-P noise line is 22–54.5 dB. Pick the 211i Max if the room figure you are matching is 674 sq ft recommended, at 16.2 lb, and you are reading a sound range of 23 to 53 dB rather than a CADR trio.

Do not add the Blueair square-foot line to the Coway square-foot line. One names a recommended room. The other names a room at 4.8 air changes per hour. The 600S-P page prints both an air-change rate and a CFM figure. Read the sentence on the page you are matching.

alternatives.title: Litter-Robot 4 alternatives in this catalogue
alternatives.description: The catalogue’s other self-cleaning litter box is the PetSafe ScoopFree Crystal Plus. This page puts the Whisker lines next to the PetSafe lines.
alternatives.subject: litter-robot-4

sections.heading: One other self-cleaning box is on the list
paragraphs: The Litter-Robot 4 page states 15 V DC, a height of 29.5 in, a footprint of 22 × 27 in, an entryway of 15.75 × 15.75 in, a weight of 24 lb empty, cleaning of up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer in a 1-cat household, and suitability for up to 4 cats. That is the full card.

The other self-cleaning litter box in the catalogue is the ScoopFree Crystal Plus. Its page states up to 30 days of cleaning, 99% dust free crystal litter, dimensions of 28.2 x 20.4 x 6.6 in, an odor line, plug-in power, and single or multi-cat households. There is not a third automatic box on this list. A fountain, a feeder, or a harness is not an alternative to a litter box.

sections.heading: Pick by height, interval, or litter type
paragraphs: Pick the Litter-Robot 4 if the interval you are matching is up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer in a 1-cat household, the household line is up to 4 cats, and the cabinet you can place is 29.5 in tall with a 22 × 27 in footprint and a 15.75 in entry. The power line is 15 V DC. The empty weight is 24 lb.

Pick the ScoopFree Crystal Plus if the cleaning line you are matching is up to 30 days, the height you can place is 6.6 in, and the litter line names crystal litter. The dimensions are 28.2 x 20.4 x 6.6 in, a lower stated height and a wider stated length than the Litter-Robot footprint. The power line says plug-in. The household line says single or multi-cat households, without a cat-count cap on that card.

The two cleaning lines are not the same chore. One names days before you empty a waste drawer for one cat. The other names days of cleaning and pairs that with a crystal-litter line. A longer stated interval is the ScoopFree line. A stated cat cap of 4 is the Litter-Robot line. The odor sentence lives only on the ScoopFree card. Read it there instead of treating it as a shared row.

The recall block is the catalogue match for each box. Neither card is a US or Canadian recall match on the check date printed below. Confirm the model name on the box against the name on the card before you buy.

worth.title: Litter-Robot 4: worth matching when these spec lines fit
worth.description: How to read the Litter-Robot 4 maker lines, height, footprint, drawer interval, and cat cap, and when the ScoopFree Crystal Plus lines are the ones that fit instead.
worth.subject: litter-robot-4

sections.heading: The question is which lines fit the room
paragraphs: Worth matching, on this page, means the maker’s lines describe the space and the chore you have. It is not a price verdict. The Litter-Robot 4 page states a height of 29.5 in, a footprint of 22 × 27 in, an entryway of 15.75 × 15.75 in, an empty weight of 24 lb, power of 15 V DC, up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer in a 1-cat household, and up to 4 cats.

If the floor opening is smaller than 22 × 27 in, or the vertical space is under 29.5 in, the cabinet line does not fit, whatever else the page says. If the household is one cat and the chore you are matching is the waste-drawer interval, the line to read is up to 8 days. If the household line you need is a stated cap, the page says up to 4 cats.

sections.heading: Pick it, or pick the lower box
paragraphs: Pick the Litter-Robot 4 if all of these are true on the page you are reading: the height is acceptable at 29.5 in, the footprint fits at 22 × 27 in, the entry is 15.75 in square, and the interval you want is the waste-drawer line for one cat. The power supply line is 15 V DC, so the card is not describing a battery tray.

Pick the ScoopFree Crystal Plus instead if the height you can give the box is 6.6 in, the cleaning line you want is up to 30 days, and the litter line you want names crystal litter. That page also states 28.2 x 20.4 x 6.6 in, plug-in power, and single or multi-cat households. It does not state an empty weight or a cat-count cap. A short cabinet and a long interval are the ScoopFree lines. A tall cabinet and an 8-day drawer line are the Litter-Robot lines.

The two pages do not share a label, so there is no single table row that decides this. Read the height first, then the interval, then the household sentence. The recall lines below are the catalogue match. Open the model page for the feed link.

worth.title: Vitamix E310: worth matching when the motor and jar lines fit
worth.description: The E310 page states a 2 HP motor, a 48 oz container, cabinet size, weight, and a 5-year warranty. The catalogue food processor is a different tool and a US recall match.
worth.subject: vitamix-e310

sections.heading: Five lines on the E310 card
paragraphs: The Vitamix E310 page states a 2 HP motor, a 48 oz container, dimensions of 9 × 8 × 18 in, a weight of 10.5 lb, and a 5-year full warranty. Worth matching means those lines describe the counter and the jar you want. A 2 HP line is a motor claim from Vitamix. An 18 in height is the cabinet line to check against the space under a cabinet.

The nearest motor appliance on the kitchen list that shares a motor label and a dimensions label is the Cuisinart Custom 14-Cup DFP-14BCNY. That page states a 14 cup bowl, a 720 W motor, dimensions of 11 in L x 7.9 in W x 14.8 in H, a 5-year motor warranty, and a 3-year limited warranty on the whole unit. A blender jar in ounces and a food-processor bowl in cups are different tools. The shared labels are only a reason to notice the difference, not a reason to treat them as the same machine.

sections.heading: Pick the blender line or stop for the recall
paragraphs: Pick the E310 if you are matching a blender, the motor line you want is 2 HP, the jar line is 48 oz, and an 18 in height at 10.5 lb fits the counter. The warranty line on that page is a 5-year full warranty. Pick it for those sentences.

Do not pick the DFP-14BCNY as a second E310. Pick that card only if you are matching a 14 cup food processor with a 720 W motor line and a lower stated height of 14.8 in. The US catalogue line for DFP-14BCNY is a recall match. The notice linked from that model page is the Conair Cuisinart food-processor recall. Read the model numbers on the notice before buying that processor. The Canadian line on the card is a separate check.
A wattage and a horsepower line are not the same unit. This page does not convert 2 HP into watts or 720 W into horsepower. The recall block below repeats the catalogue status for each model.

worth.title: Sony WH-1000XM5: worth matching when the battery and weight lines fit
worth.description: The Sony specifications page states weight, charge time, and battery life for the WH-1000XM5. The Bose QuietComfort Ultra page states a shorter battery line and a shorter charge line.
worth.subject: sony-wh-1000xm5

sections.heading: The lines that answer a headphone match
paragraphs: The Sony specifications page states a weight of about 8.82 oz, a charge time of about 3.5 hours, and battery life of max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on or max. 40 hours with it off. The product page also states the model WH-1000XM5, that 2 processors control 8 microphones, and multipoint. Worth matching means you are buying that model and those battery and weight lines are the ones you meant to match.

The QuietComfort Ultra specifications table states up to 24 hours, a weight of 0.56 lb, and a 3 hour charge, plus Quiet, Aware, and Immersion modes, multipoint for two devices, and Bose Immersive Audio. The weight units differ: ounces on the Sony page, pounds on the Bose page. This page does not convert them.

sections.heading: Pick the longer battery line or the shorter charge line
paragraphs: Pick the WH-1000XM5 if the battery line you are matching is max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on, or max. 40 hours with it off, and the weight line you are matching is about 8.82 oz. The charge line that goes with that page is about 3.5 hours. Pick it if the microphone sentence, 2 processors and 8 microphones, is the noise-cancelling description you meant.

Pick the QuietComfort Ultra if the battery line you are matching is up to 24 hours, the charge line is 3 hours, and the mode line names Quiet, Aware, and Immersion. A shorter stated charge time is the Bose line. A longer stated playback line with noise cancelling on is the Sony line. Multipoint appears on both cards, with the Bose card adding “two devices.”

Neither card is a US or Canadian recall match on the catalogue date below. Confirm WH-1000XM5 on the box if that is the model you are buying. The Bose card is a different model with its own battery sentence. The comparison page for this pair repeats only the labels both cards share, which are battery, weight, and charge time, and it leaves the microphone line and the mode line on the separate cards.
